verdict.rationale: Square documents a broad public API surface that lets a programmatic user drive core business operations: Catalog, Inventory, Locations, Disputes, Payouts, Terminal and Payments. It also ships official SDKs in TypeScript, .NET, Java, Python, Ruby and PHP, an API Explorer for direct calls, a sandbox, and a published API specification repository. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of API usage, and a machine-readable OpenAPI spec at a standard discoverable path (probes returned 404).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Learn about creating and managing a seller's item library (also known as a catalog) with the Catalog API.
Learn about using the Inventory API to adjust inventory quantities and review inventory changes for items in a Square catalog.
You can call Square APIs directly from [API Explorer](https://developer.squareup.com/explorer/square) to test their capabilities and perform actions on objects within a Square account.
The Square TypeScript library provides convenient access to the Square APIs from TypeScript.
The Disputes API allows a seller to use your application to complete the steps of the disputes process.
The Square Sandbox is a free, isolated server environment that allows developers to safely test Square APIs without affecting real data.
